_comment: The one gBCE re-run the owner approved on 2026-10-05, after the O-25 contamination finding.
ADR 0016 chose BCE over gBCE for SASRec v1 on pilot-6pct.json: BCE run 0c600f9d... read
warm recall@500 0.3186 and gBCE run fb63a3ae96c64205ba5e57e5ca4b0611 read 0.2937. Both read
the contaminated 6% split (cutoff 1471288304; its holdout was all sealed-window data).
This cell is pilot6-gbce-t0.5-neg32 exactly as that run logged it (gbce, calibration_t 0.5,
32 negatives, 2 epochs, exact retrieval, seed 42, every other field at its default), with
two differences the protocol imposes rather than chooses: the O-25 cut (the 6% sample is
split at the full split's boundaries, cutoff 1466837397, holdout_end 1469256597), and the
objective of record named explicitly. The gBCE beta is recomputed from this split's train
catalog, as the trainer always does. Like WO-1's pilots, it runs with PR #162's evaluation
fix, which the September pair predates.
Compared with WO-1's BCE seed-42 pilot 7baeb7d0b812486e9c86fdd3435ea715 (warm recall@500
0.3625487076, same seed, same protocol) and the four-seed BCE range [0.3611, 0.3936].
